stem_book: For a quadratic expression ax² + bx + c, a < 0, c > 0, b > 0, which of the following best represents the graph of y = ax² + bx + c? (a) (b) (c) (d) [the four options are graph sketches of downward parabolas — see figure]
reason: Manifest's verbal descriptions of the option graphs are inaccurate ((b) actually has a non-positive y-intercept); options are drawings, use the figure.
work: a<0 downward; vertex −b/2a > 0 (right of y-axis); c > 0 positive y-intercept; c/a < 0 → roots of opposite sign = (c)
